misconception.text: The speed of light in vacuum is different for observers moving at different speeds.

correction.text: It is the same for every inertial observer, whatever the motion of the source or the observer. That is Einstein's second postulate, and it is why there is no absolute rest.

signal.text: Our own question offers the observer-dependent reading as an option.

misconception.text: A clock moving at a high speed ticks faster for an observer who sees it moving.

correction.text: It ticks more slowly. Time dilation means the moving clock runs slow as measured in the frame in which it is moving, and each of two inertial observers sees the other's clock run slow.

signal.text: Our own question offers the faster reading as an option.
